note.note:
Action Plan:
1. Treat as probable acute uncomplicated cystitis: start empiric antibiotic therapy (choices discussed: trimethoprim OR nitrofurantoin). Note: dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript.
2. Provide a midstream urine sample today — sample to be dropped off at practice; urine sent to lab for testing/culture; results will be communicated to patient.
3. Symptomatic care: advise increased oral fluids and regular paracetamol for pain as needed.
4. Safety net / follow-up: return or contact clinician if any of fever, flank/back pain, or vomiting develop; if symptoms not improving after ~1 week, re-assessment in clinic.
5. Sexual health / pregnancy considerations: patient is sexually active with recent unprotected intercourse (~1 week ago to 2 weeks ago) and last menstrual period 2 weeks ago — clinician noted to bear pregnancy in mind if symptoms do not improve. No pregnancy test was ordered during this consult (see Quality checks).
6. Documented allergy: avoid clindamycin (patient-reported prior adverse reaction).
7. Administrative: arrange for patient to drop urine sample at one of the practices for immediate testing and laboratory send-off; clinician will contact patient with results.
8. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint:
  - 19-year-old female (Amanda Jackson) with ~<1 week of dysuria (burning/stinging on micturition), increased urinary frequency, and lower abdominal / suprapubic aching that is worse with voiding.
  - Noted pink-tinged urine today (patient-reported hematuria).
- Onset/duration/progression:
  - Symptoms started just under one week ago and are interfering with university attendance.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Denies fever, chills, flank/back pain, nausea, vomiting.
  - No abnormal vaginal discharge reported.
- Sexual history:
  - Sexually active with long-term boyfriend; generally does not use condoms.
  - Last unprotected intercourse approximately 1–2 weeks ago.
  - Last menstrual period 2 weeks ago.
- Past medical history:
  - Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
- Medications:
  - Combined oral contraceptive pill (type: combined pill).
  - Takes an IBS medication (name begins with "M"; dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies:
  - Adverse reaction to clindamycin (reported).
- Social history:
  - University student living in halls with a flatmate.
  - Tried cannabis once ~1.5 weeks ago; does not smoke tobacco; occasional alcohol.

Objective:
- No vital signs or physical examination recorded in the transcript.
- No point-of-care urinalysis or laboratory results available at time of consult.
- Mental state: patient conversationally appropriate and able to provide history.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Dysuria / Suspected acute uncomplicated cystitis:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated cystitis (bacterial UTI) — High likelihood (DDx: "Acute uncomplicated cystitis (bacterial UTI)" — High).
   - Differential diagnosis (consistent with DDx):
     - Urethritis due to sexually transmitted infection (Chlamydia/Gonorrhea) — Medium likelihood.
     - Urolithiasis (renal/ureteric stone) — Low to medium likelihood.
     - Acute pyelonephritis (ascending UTI) — Low likelihood (no fever or flank pain).
     - Interstitial cystitis / painful bladder syndrome — Low likelihood (typically chronic).
     - Bladder neoplasm — very unlikely in this age group (noted in DDx as rare).
   - Investigations planned:
     - Midstream urine sample for laboratory testing and culture (organised by practice; patient to drop off sample).
     - No point-of-care urinalysis or STI NAATs were ordered during this consult (see Quality checks).
   - Treatment planned:
     - Empiric antibiotic therapy discussed: trimethoprim OR nitrofurantoin (patient to start antibiotic). Dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript.
     - Advise increased oral fluids / hydration.
     - Paracetamol for symptomatic pain control as needed.
   - Relevant referrals:
     - None at this time. Reassess and consider further investigation/referral if symptoms worsen or do not improve.

2. Possible sexually transmitted urethritis (STI-related urethritis):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Urethritis due to STI (eg. Chlamydia trachomatis / Neisseria gonorrhoeae) — Medium likelihood (DDx item: "Urethritis due to STI" — Medium).
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Isolated urethral chlamydia or gonorrhea may present with dysuria +/- minimal discharge.
   - Investigations planned:
     - No STI testing ordered during this visit per transcript. Consider NAAT testing (urine or urethral/vaginal swab) if symptoms persist, if urine culture is negative, or if clinical suspicion increases.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Not specifically treated for STI during this consult; empiric UTI antibiotics were discussed. If STI testing performed and positive, treat per guidelines.

3. Pregnancy consideration:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Pregnancy not suspected by patient (on combined pill; LMP 2 weeks ago) but should be considered if symptoms persist or if clinical concern arises (DDx includes pregnancy-related urinary changes).
   - Investigations planned:
     - No pregnancy test was performed during this consult. Consider pregnancy test if clinically indicated or if symptoms persist.

4. IBS (past medical history; not an active issue for current presentation):
   - Assessment: IBS documented as past medical history; bowel symptoms reported as chronic and unchanged.
   - No specific investigations or treatment changes related to IBS during this consult.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vital signs documented (temperature, pulse) — relevant to assess for systemic infection.
  - No physical abdominal/flank examination was performed or documented.
  - No urine dipstick or urinalysis result documented at point of care.
  - No urine culture result available yet (sample to be sent).
  - No pregnancy test was performed despite recent unprotected intercourse and LMP 2 weeks ago.
  - No STI testing (NAAT) was ordered in the consult despite recent unprotected sex — clinician did not explicitly order these tests.
  - Antibiotic name chosen but dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Exact name and dose of the IBS medication not documented.
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None identified — DDx is consistent with the clinician’s assessment of probable uncomplicated cystitis and lists relevant differentials.
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio/content clear overall; minor brief interruptions and conversational speech present but history is interpretable and key clinical details were documented.
